title: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi
text: PM Kisan is a central income-support scheme for eligible farmer families. Beneficiaries are selected by state/UT authorities; the money is transferred to the bank account linked to the beneficiary's Aadhaar. To check status, use the official PM Kisan beneficiary portal or the nearest CSC/block agriculture office. Keep Aadhaar, bank passbook, land records and the registration number ready. Installment dates and amounts change; do not trust forwarded messages. Verify on the official portal.

title: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
text: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY provides health cover for eligible families at empanelled hospitals. Check eligibility with the official PM-JAY portal or the nearest CSC/Arogya Mitra. Usually Aadhaar, ration card/family details and a mobile number are needed. At the hospital, ask for the Ayushman desk and verify that the hospital is empanelled before treatment. Coverage amounts and empanelment lists change; confirm on the official site.

title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
text: PMFBY insures notified crops against yield loss from natural calamities, pests and disease. Enrol through the official PMFBY portal, a bank, a CSC or the insurance company listed for your state, before the notified cut-off date. For a claim, report the loss to the insurance company, bank or agriculture office and keep photos of the damaged crop with location/date. Cut-off dates and premium rates vary by state and crop; verify on the official portal.

title: Mudra loan (PMMY)
text: Mudra loans support small non-farm businesses under Shishu, Kishor and Tarun categories. Apply at a bank, NBFC or the official Jan Samarth portal. Keep KYC, business proof/plan, bank statement and quotations for machinery or stock. The bank decides the amount and interest rate; do not pay an agent for a guarantee. Verify eligibility and current limits with the lender or the official portal.

title: PM Awas Yojana (Gramin/Urban)
text: PMAY provides housing assistance to eligible families. Rural applications go through the Gram Panchayat and the AwaasSoft portal; urban applications go through the municipal body or the official PMAY-U portal. Keep Aadhaar, income certificate, land documents and bank details. Survey/verification is required; an application alone does not guarantee a house. Check the beneficiary list on the official portal.
verify: Gram Panchayat / municipal office / official portal

title: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana
text: Ujjwala provides LPG connections to eligible women from poor households. Apply at the nearest LPG distributor or the official Ujjwala portal with Aadhaar, address proof, bank account and a recent photograph. The distributor verifies eligibility. Subsidy and connection rules change; confirm the current process with the distributor or official site.

title: Jan Dhan account
text: A Jan Dhan account is a basic savings account with no minimum balance, opened at any bank branch or Bank Mitra/CSC. Carry Aadhaar (or other KYC) and a photograph. It can receive government benefits and is linked to a RuPay card. Mobile number seeding is needed for SMS alerts. Check the account status at the bank; do not share the OTP or PIN with anyone.

title: Ration card / PDS
text: Ration card applications and corrections are handled by the state food/civil supplies department, usually at the block office, tehsil or CSC. Keep Aadhaar of family members, address proof, income certificate and the existing ration card. Adding a newborn or a new family member requires a separate form and verification. Entitlements differ by state and category; check the state portal or the ration office.

title: MGNREGA job card
text: MGNREGA guarantees up to 100 days of unskilled wage work per rural household per year, subject to demand and availability. Apply for a job card at the Gram Panchayat with family details, Aadhaar and residence proof. Ask for a dated receipt. If work is not provided within the statutory time, you can raise a grievance with the gram panchayat, block programme officer or the official NREGA portal. Wage rates and timelines are set by law/state; verify locally.
verify: Gram Panchayat / block office / NREGA portal

title: Kisan Credit Card
text: KCC gives farmers short-term credit for inputs and cultivation. Apply at a bank with Aadhaar, land records/tenancy proof, crop details and passport photos. The bank assesses the credit limit based on land, crop and repayment history. Interest subvention/waiver rules change; ask the branch for the current terms and read the sanction letter before signing.

title: Soil Health Card
text: The Soil Health Card scheme provides soil test results and nutrient recommendations. Contact the local agriculture department, KVK or soil testing lab; samples are usually collected through a camp or block office. The card reports pH, organic carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium and micronutrients, with crop-wise fertilizer advice. Follow the card and a KVK/agri officer's recommendation rather than a fixed NPK dose.

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
text: Sukanya Samriddhi is a small-savings scheme for a girl child below 10 years. Open it at a post office or authorised bank with the child's birth certificate, guardian KYC and address proof. Deposits earn a government-declared interest rate; the account matures after the specified period. Interest rates and rules change every quarter/year; confirm with the post office/bank or the official India Post/NSI site.

title: Atal Pension Yojana
text: Atal Pension Yojana is a government pension scheme for subscribed workers aged 18-40. The subscriber chooses a pension amount; contributions continue until 60. Apply at a bank or post office with Aadhaar, savings account and mobile number. Auto-debit mandates the contribution. Tax rules and eligibility can change; confirm with the bank and the official PFRDA site.

title: e-Shram card
text: e-Shram is a national registration card for unorganised workers. Register free at the official e-Shram portal or a CSC with Aadhaar, mobile number, bank details and occupation. The card gives a UAN and access to welfare updates; it is not a guarantee of a pension or cash transfer. Beware of agents charging a fee. Verify benefits on the official portal.

title: Aadhaar update
text: Aadhaar updates (address, mobile, name, DOB) are done at an authorised Aadhaar centre or the official UIDAI portal. For address, carry a valid proof; for biometric updates, the enrollee must be present. Fees are fixed by UIDAI; demand a receipt. Never share the Aadhaar OTP with an agent. Check status on the UIDAI portal.

title: Tomato leaf yellowing and blight
text: Yellowing tomato leaves can come from waterlogging, nitrogen deficiency, early blight, leaf curl virus or whitefly damage. Ask for a photo of the upper and lower leaf and the whole plant. Safe first steps: remove badly affected leaves and dispose away from the field; water in the morning and improve drainage; stake plants for airflow; use sticky traps for whitefly; avoid overhead irrigation. Do not spray a pesticide without a label and a KVK/agri officer's confirmation. For persistent patches, take a sample to the nearest KVK.

title: Potato leaf curl and blight
text: Potato leaves curling or wilting can indicate aphid/whitefly-transmitted virus, late blight, heat stress or water stress. Check the underside for aphids, and look for dark water-soaked patches after cool humid weather. Remove infected plants, avoid overhead watering, keep good spacing, and use certified seed. Late blight needs a fungicide recommendation from a KVK/agri officer; do not guess a dose. Store seed tubers in a cool, ventilated, dark place.

title: Wheat irrigation and yellowing
text: Wheat needs critical irrigation at crown-root initiation, tillering, jointing, flowering and grain filling; the exact schedule depends on soil and weather. Yellowing can be nitrogen deficiency, waterlogging, rust or a root problem. Check soil moisture by hand, improve drainage, and avoid a blanket urea top-dress without a soil test. For rust, take a photo and contact the KVK; do not spray without a recommendation.

title: Rice yellowing and pest checks
text: Rice yellowing can be nitrogen deficiency, iron chlorosis, brown planthopper, bacterial leaf blight or water stress. Check the base of the plant for hoppers and look for lesions on the leaf. Maintain shallow water, avoid excess nitrogen, and keep field bunds clean. For planthopper, drain the field and contact the KVK before any insecticide. Do not mix multiple pesticides.

title: Safe crop-problem triage
text: For any crop symptom, first get a clear photo of the affected part, the underside of the leaf and the whole plant, plus the crop age, soil type, irrigation and recent inputs. Check for waterlogging, drought, nutrient deficiency and pests before spraying anything. Remove and destroy badly affected plant parts, keep the field ventilated, and use safe IPM steps (sticky traps, neem oil per label) first. Never use human medicine or an unlabeled pesticide on crops. Confirm the diagnosis with a KVK/agri officer.

title: Fever safety
text: For fever, rest, drink water/ORS and monitor temperature. Do not self-prescribe antibiotics or a medicine dose. Seek a doctor/ASHA urgently for a baby under 3 months, fever over 3 days, breathing difficulty, chest pain, fits, confusion or fainting. For a child, use light clothing and keep hydrating; do not give aspirin to children. Call 108 for an emergency. This is general safety information, not a diagnosis.
source: WHO/National Health Portal guidance - verify with a clinician

title: Diarrhoea and ORS
text: For diarrhoea, give ORS little and often. One ORS packet is mixed in the amount of clean water printed on the packet; do not use extra sugar or salt. Continue breastfeeding for infants. Seek care urgently for blood in stool, no urine, sunken eyes, severe weakness, high fever or a lethargic child. Do not take an antibiotic or anti-motility medicine without a doctor. Call 108 if the person is unconscious or shocked.
source: WHO/National Health Portal guidance - verify with a clinician

title: Snake bite first response
text: For a snake bite, call 108 or take the person to the nearest hospital immediately. Keep the person calm and still, remove rings/tight items, and keep the bitten limb at rest. Do not cut, suck, burn the wound or apply a tight tourniquet. Do not give alcohol or home remedies. Note the time of the bite and any symptoms (breathing difficulty, drooping eyelids, bleeding). Antivenom is a hospital treatment.
source: WHO/National Health Portal guidance - verify with a clinician

title: Live data rule
text: The assistant cannot see live mandi prices, weather, train status, exam dates, scheme installments or cricket scores. When asked, it must say it cannot check live data, name the official source (eNAM/mandi board, IMD, NTES/IRCTC, official exam portal, PM Kisan portal, Cricbuzz/TV), and give the next step. It must not invent a number, date or price.

title: Tamatar ke patte peele - Hinglish
text: Bhai, tamatar ke patte peele hone ki wajah paani/nutrient ki kami, keede, ya fungal bimari ho sakti hai. Pehle ek saaf photo bhejiye — patte ke upar aur neeche dono side, aur paudhe ka poora hissa. Tab tak affected patte hata kar khet se door dispose karein, paani subah dein, hawa aane dein, aur sticky trap ya neem oil label ke hisaab se try karein. Koi bhi pesticide bina KVK/agri officer ki salah ke na chhidkein. Sahi wajah ke liye nazdiki KVK se sample dikhayein.

title: Fasal ki samasya - safe steps
text: Kisi bhi fasal ki samasya mein pehle saaf photo lein — affected patte ke upar aur neeche, paudhe ka poora hissa, aur mitti/paani ki jankari. Paani ki kami ya zyada paani, nutrient ki kami, keede aur fungal bimari common wajah hain. Safe steps: affected hisse hata kar khet se door dispose karein, drainage aur hawa theek karein, sticky trap/neem oil label ke hisaab se use karein. Bina KVK/agri officer ki salah ke pesticide na chhidkein.
